title: RB-013 hi 'Covers Presentation.' recurrence is NOT a TM-caching or model-quality issue: the accepted, receipted, on-disk file diverges from what the SAME accepted attempt flushed to L2 TM
supersedes_partial_hypothesis_in: data/summaries/fp-glued-identifier-recurrence-pdfgeneratedpython-20260911.json is a different bug (Aspose.PDF brand-dot-term, unrelated) -- this record is standalone, not an update to that one. This record's OWN earlier hypothesis this same session (recorded in taskcard_status.json wake summaries, not a separate fp file) -- 'TM already has the correct value, the committed file just never got it, a replace retrigger should fix it' -- is CONFIRMED WRONG by this investigation. Recording the correction here rather than silently discarding it.
evidence_chain: wwpc-hi-rb013-combined-20260912r3 (campaign_id) ran to completion: status=COMPLETE, 2/2 accepted, 0 failed, attempt_model_outcomes.professionalize_llm.'3'.accepted=2 (succeeded on the 3rd labeled attempt).
acceptance_receipts.jsonl for both cells: campaign_attempt=3, attempt_model_id=professionalize_llm, all 44 gates passed=true, output_sha256 recorded.

Computed sha256 of the ACTUAL on-disk files directly: both match output_sha256 from the receipts EXACTLY -- ruling out any post-acceptance overwrite. The file IS what the pipeline itself wrote and receipted as final.
Both on-disk files still have the frontmatter description's trailing sentence 'Covers Presentation.' left entirely in English -- the identical defect from before this retrigger.

Queried L2 TM directly for the exact same (source_text, hi, campaign=wwpc-hi-rb013-combined-20260912r3) keys: BOTH have a fully correct Hindi translation of the COMPLETE two-sentence description, including 'Covers Presentation.' correctly rendered as 'प्रस्तुति को कवर करता है।' / 'कवर करता है: प्रस्तुति।'. Decoded and verified the actual string (not assumed from truncated output).

Therefore: within the SAME accepted attempt (campaign_attempt=3) of the SAME campaign run, the text that got flushed to TM and the text that got written into the final reconstructed document are DIFFERENT STRINGS for the same translation unit.
ruled_out: Model quality/Hindi-specific weakness: DISPROVEN -- the model demonstrably produced a fully correct translation (found in TM) on the very attempt that got accepted. This is not RB-013's 'single-locale model variance' pattern; retrying on a different model will not fix a reconstruction-layer bug regardless of translation quality.

TM cache staleness / needing a 'replace' retrigger to pick up an old-but-correct value: DISPROVEN by this session's own experiment -- a fresh replace retrigger reproduced a FRESH correct TM entry (new campaign_id in the key) and STILL wrote the wrong file. The bug is not about consuming a stale cache; it reproduces on every fresh run.
Post-write corruption/overwrite by another process: DISPROVEN by exact sha256 match between the receipt's output_sha256 and the live on-disk file.
leading_hypothesis_not_yet_confirmed: src/workers/campaign_runner.py's multi-attempt retry structure (~line 2251-2305: primary phase carries an internal retry_budget of up to `primary_attempts - 1` guided retries within ONE translate_file() call, all labeled with the same campaign_attempt number for audit purposes) may reconcile the 'winning' translation and the TM flush from two different internal retry iterations -- e.g. an early internal retry's (possibly still-bad) in-memory translation result object gets used for final document reconstruction, while a LATER internal retry's (corrected) output is what actually gets flushed to TM under the umbrella 'attempt 3' label. This has NOT been confirmed by reading the actual retry-then-reconstruct code path in translate_file() / the segment_translator plumbing -- flagged as the next concrete place to look, not asserted as proven.
diagnostic_in_progress: Launched wwpc-hi-rb013-m2m-diag-20260912(r2) targeting the same 2 cells with --primary-model m2m100_418m after purging TM. Per src/workers/campaign_runner.py's own comment (_primary_backend_is_deterministic), a deterministic non-LLM primary backend gets primary_retry_budget=0 -- i.e. exactly ONE real invocation, no internal guided retries. If m2m100 produces a CORRECT file on its single attempt, that is strong evidence the bug is specific to the multi-attempt reconciliation path (supporting the hypothesis above). If m2m100 ALSO produces a wrong file despite a correct TM entry, the bug is broader than the retry path and lives somewhere more fundamental in reconstruction. Result not yet known as of this record's writing -- check campaign wwpc-hi-rb013-m2m-diag-20260912r2's outcome before drawing conclusions.
why_not_fixed_this_session: Confirming the exact mechanism requires tracing translate_file()'s internal retry loop and the segment-to-document reconstruction assembly (likely in src/workers/campaign_runner.py past line 2305, or in the segment_translator/reconstructor modules it calls into) -- a substantially larger investigation than the 2 code fixes already landed this session (7dceae31 i18n table-header registry gap, 01756e5d dirty-scope exemption gap). Time-boxed this investigation to gathering conclusive evidence and narrowing the search space rather than completing the fix, to keep this mission-loop iteration bounded.
recommended_next_action: A future iteration (or a dedicated Track-B taskcard) should: (1) check the m2m100 diagnostic's outcome first -- it may already answer whether this is retry-path-specific; (2) if still needed, instrument or step through translate_file()'s guided-retry loop for a case that needs >1 internal attempt, comparing the TranslationResult object that gets returned/used for reconstruction against the TM-flushed value at each retry iteration; (3) given the severity (any historically 'accepted' cell that needed retries could carry silently-wrong content that reads as fluent, grammatical target-language text and passes all 44 structural gates), consider a portfolio-wide audit cross-referencing TM values against committed file content for any cell whose acceptance_receipts.jsonl shows campaign_attempt > 1 or attempt_model_id indicating an escalation -- this defect class would NOT be caught by any existing automated gate, only by body-review or exactly this kind of TM-vs-file diff.

addendum_m2m_diagnostic_result.result: wwpc-hi-rb013-m2m-diag-20260912r3 completed: m2m100_418m was REJECTED on both cells (0/2, escalated after failing its own attempts), then professionalize_llm's LLM-escalation phase (labeled campaign_attempt=4) ACCEPTED both. addendum_m2m_diagnostic_result.correction_to_ruled_out_claim: IMPORTANT: this result means the claim in this record's own 'ruled_out' section -- 'it reproduces on every fresh run' -- is TOO STRONG and should be read as 'reproduced on 2 of 3 observed fresh-generation attempts so far,' not deterministically on every run. The bug is evidently intermittent / attempt-path-dependent, not a fixed deterministic divergence. This is still consistent with (and arguably strengthens) the leading hypothesis about multi-attempt reconciliation -- non-determinism across different attempt counts/paths is exactly what a retry-object-selection bug would produce -- but it means a simple 'always fails' test case cannot be relied on to validate any future fix; reproduction requires triggering the SAME internal retry path/attempt count each time, which is not yet controllable from outside campaign_runner.py.
